issues.problem: English adds a fact not in the Chinese: "from the king on down no one could get it for her" (i.e., the king and all below tried and failed to avenge her father). The Chinese only says she was unable to take revenge for three years.
issues.suggestion: Delete "and from the king on down no one could get it for her", or add the equivalent to the Chinese line.

issues.problem: English adds the place name "at Ye" ("hold the army at Ye in wait-and-see"); the Chinese only says 魏王使人止晋鄙留军观望 with no location.
issues.suggestion: Drop "at Ye", or add 驻于邺 (or 邺) to the Chinese.

issues.problem: English adds the self-question "Had he fallen short somewhere?", a doubt not stated in the Chinese (which goes straight from the grievance to turning back).
issues.suggestion: Delete the sentence, or add the matching doubt (自己是否有所失) to the Chinese.

issues.problem: English adds two elements absent from the Chinese: the gloss "the eastern gate of Daliang" for the Yimen, and the intent "testing his host" after "without yielding it" (Chinese only 不让).
issues.suggestion: Trim to "kept the Yimen" and "without yielding it", or add the gloss/testing intent to the Chinese.

issues.problem: English adds "caps of office" to the procession image; the Chinese has only 车盖接连不断 (carriage canopies in an unbroken line).
issues.suggestion: Change to "carriage canopies in an unbroken line".

overall: The two editions agree on all facts, dates, numbers, names, quotations, attributions and hedges; the only mismatches are a few details the English adds that the Chinese does not have (two of them factual: the failed search for Lady Ruji's father's killer and the location "at Ye").
